c74object.name: bob~
c74object.digest: Moog analog lowpass resonant filter simulation
c74object.description:
bob~ imitates a Moog transistor ladder resonant filter. It uses Runge-Kutta numerical integration to solve the differential equations describing the analog circuit dynamics.
This implementation is based on the original design by Miller Puckette for Pure Data. It provides an authentic nonlinear response, especially at high resonance levels where the transistor saturation characteristics shape the sound.
The filter is oversampled to ensure stability and high-frequency accuracy.

objarg.name: cutoff
objarg.description: Sets the initial cutoff frequency in Hz. Default is 500 Hz.

objarg.name: resonance
objarg.description: Sets the initial resonance amount (typically 0 to 4). Default is 0.5.

inlet.description: Cutoff frequency in Hz. Can be controlled by a signal or a float message.
Resonance amount. Usually stable up to 4.0. Above 4.0, the filter will self-oscillate.

attribute.name: oversample
attribute.description: Sets the internal oversampling factor (default is 2). Higher values improve accuracy and stability at high frequencies at the cost of higher CPU usage.

attribute.name: saturation
attribute.description: Sets the saturation level of the transistor simulation. Default value is 3.0. Lower values increase the nonlinear distortion within the filter ladder.

method.name: clear
method.description: Resets the internal state variables (capacitors) to zero. Useful to stop feedback or clear NaNs if the filter explodes.
